market-research-v15.json.summary: Approve bounded stock-coverage and buyer price-gap routing responses, while retaining the current operating policy and profile parameters. Stockouts (49 in 60 minutes) and 48 units of stock versus 198 median peer stock support a coverage response, though external trade rate is essentially flat and a discoverability block is recorded. Goods conversion is weak (5/43 closed orders paid) and 61/62 goods quotes were above cap; route qualifying repeated failures to recovery probes without changing the cap. Do not promote a challenger: evaluation is not ready and has only 9 paid challenger outcomes. The quality holdout is predictive, not causal, and official stars-rank mapping is unverified.
hypotheses: A bounded repeat-demand coverage response may reduce stockouts, subject to live supply, cash, and refund guards; flat external trade rate and the discoverability block are counterevidence to expanding inventory broadly.

Routing repeated, term-comparable goods price failures to recovery probes may improve learning without changing the price cap; above-cap quotes alone do not establish that any revised offer will convert.
The holdout predictive improvement does not establish causal star gains or verify the official stars-rank mapping.

shop-plan-v15.json.note: Preview is not a supply authorization; fresh guards remain authoritative.

research-last-result.summary: Approve bounded stock-coverage and buyer price-gap routing responses, while retaining the current operating policy and profile parameters. Stockouts (49 in 60 minutes) and 48 units of stock versus 198 median peer stock support a coverage response, though external trade rate is essentially flat and a discoverability block is recorded. Goods conversion is weak (5/43 closed orders paid) and 61/62 goods quotes were above cap; route qualifying repeated failures to recovery probes without changing the cap. Do not promote a challenger: evaluation is not ready and has only 9 paid challenger outcomes. The quality holdout is predictive, not causal, and official stars-rank mapping is unverified.
hypotheses: A bounded repeat-demand coverage response may reduce stockouts, subject to live supply, cash, and refund guards; flat external trade rate and the discoverability block are counterevidence to expanding inventory broadly.

Routing repeated, term-comparable goods price failures to recovery probes may improve learning without changing the price cap; above-cap quotes alone do not establish that any revised offer will convert.
The holdout predictive improvement does not establish causal star gains or verify the official stars-rank mapping.

market_research_published.summary: Keep current parameters and wait on supply-plan or operating changes: the operating regime is unverified, facts and supply guards need refreshing, and results are unattributed. Low stock and recent stockouts warrant rechecking after guards are current, but do not justify an operating intent now. Goods quotes were all above cap in the small recent sample; do not infer broader demand or change price caps. Challenger results are promising but not promotion-ready.
hypotheses: Low stock may be contributing to observed stockouts; verify with fresh supply guards before testing a coverage response.
Goods contract conversion may be limited by above-cap quotes; assess again with refreshed facts, without relaxing price caps.
The challenger’s higher observed reward is inconclusive: it has 111 completed samples and 9 paid, and evaluation says it is not ready.

market_research_published.summary: Maintain current buyer settings and the diversified supply plan. Fresh feedback shows low stock (66 units versus 228.5 median peer stock) and 9 stockouts, supporting a bounded stock-coverage response despite slightly softer external trade activity. Goods contract conversion is weak (11/142 paid; 229/233 quotes above cap), but this does not support changing price caps or claim that broader probing will fix the gap. Challenger evidence is not mature; quality holdout remains shadow-only with unverified stars mapping.
hypotheses: A bounded increase in repeat-demand stock coverage may reduce stockouts; validate against subsequent stockout and sales data.
Goods contract failures may be driven by price-cap mismatch: 229/233 goods quotes exceed cap, so quote diversity or probing alone may not resolve them.
The challenger reward estimate is higher than champion's, but 9 paid outcomes and no mature canonical results are insufficient for economic promotion.

market_research_published.summary: Use the diversified supply plan and authorize a bounded stock-coverage operating response: inventory is 62 units versus a 281.5-unit median among online peers, with 22 stockouts in the last 60 minutes. External trading has softened (20-minute rate ratio 0.885), so this supports targeted coverage, not an aggressive expansion. Keep buyer settings at 8% / gap power 2 / non-diverse quotes; goods conversion is weak and all recent goods quotes were above cap. Do not promote the challenger: its 111 closed and 9 paid outcomes are insufficient for mature evaluation. Keep the rating model in shadow; the official stars mapping is unverified.
hypotheses: Low stock and recorded stockouts support testing a bounded increase in repeat-demand coverage, while the recent decline in external trade argues against broad expansion.
Goods contract performance may be constrained by the price frontier: all 20 recent goods quotes were above cap; this does not justify changing the price cap.
The challenger’s higher observed reward is not conclusive with 111 closed samples and 9 paid; mature promotion criteria are unmet.

market_research_published.summary: Keep buyer parameters at 8% probes, gap power 2, and non-diverse quotes; goods quotes are all above cap, so test only bounded same-owner/category recovery routing without relaxing caps. Authorize bounded repeat-demand stock coverage because 22 stockouts and 62 units of stock versus a 117-unit peer median indicate a measurable coverage gap, but retain the diversified plan only subject to fresh supply guards. Do not promote the challenger: its evaluation is not ready, and quality holdout mapping is unverified. Transport/discoverability blocks and a recent external-trade rate ratio of 0.856 counsel against broader shop changes.
hypotheses: Same-owner/category routing of failed goods contracts with recovery probes may improve conversion without changing price caps; mature causal buyer evidence is absent.
Bounded repeat-demand coverage may reduce stockouts, though the external trade slowdown and discoverability blocks could limit shop benefit.
The quality holdout's lower MSE does not establish star-rank or causal improvement.

market_research_published.summary: Use a bounded stock-coverage operating response, but defer policy and parameter changes: inventory is 58 units versus 153 median online-peer stock, with 27 stockouts and 9 own paid sales in 60 minutes. Supply execution still requires fresh guards, and the shop is reported nondiscoverable. Goods conversion remains weak, with 1/23 closed orders paid and all 40 goods quotes above cap; do not relax price caps. The challenger is not promotion-ready, and the rating holdout is predictive rather than causal with rank mapping unverified.
hypotheses: A bounded repeat-demand stock response may reduce stockouts, subject to live supply and cash/refund guards.
Goods outcomes may be constrained by above-cap quotes; same-owner/category routing with recovery probes could be measured without changing price caps.
The challenger’s higher observed reward is not sufficient evidence for promotion: evaluator readiness is false and mature canonical buyer results are absent.

market_research_published.summary: Allow bounded stock-coverage and buyer price-gap routing responses: recent stockouts are high, while goods quotes repeatedly exceed the price cap. Keep research parameters and operating policy unchanged; do not promote the challenger because mature canonical results are absent and the evaluation is not ready. Transport issues and declining external-trade rate argue against broader inventory changes.
hypotheses: Coverage response may reduce stockouts, although external trade rate is 0.89 of the prior 40-minute rate and does not support a larger coverage commitment.
Goods conversion may be constrained by the price frontier: all 50 recent goods quotes were above cap, with 1 of 29 closed orders paid; routing probes can test recovery without changing the cap.

Economic promotion remains unsupported: challenger evaluation has 114 closed and 9 paid, is not ready, and canonical mature results are absent; the quality surrogate also does not verify official stars-rank mapping.

market_research_published.summary: Market activity is substantial but easing (786 trades in 20 minutes; rate ratio 0.906). Own stock is low versus peers (50 vs median 191) with 39 stockouts, supporting bounded coverage routing. Food conversion exceeds goods (50/88 vs 3/32 closed orders), while goods quotes are frequently above cap (53/54). Keep the operating policy unchanged; do not promote the challenger, infer demand from observational preferences, or change price caps. The holdout is predictive but noncausal, and official stars-rank mapping is unverified.
hypotheses: Increasing repeat-demand coverage beyond one cycle may reduce stockouts, but first measure the bounded response against paid sales, margin, and stockouts.
For repeated term-comparable price failures, same-owner/category recovery probes may recover some buyer orders without changing caps; verify closed-order results.
Goods price feasibility may constrain conversion, but the available quotes and conversion data do not establish a viable alternative price.

market_research_published.summary: Stockouts (39 in 60 minutes) and inventory below the online-peer median support bounded stock-coverage and eligible failed-contract routing responses, subject to live supply checks. Retain the diversified shop plan and current operating policy: market trade rate is near flat, while transport and discoverability blockers remain. Goods conversion is weak and most goods quotes exceed the cap; recovery probes must not relax price caps. Challenger promotion is unsupported: evaluation is not ready and canonical mature buyer outcomes are absent.
hypotheses: Bounded repeat-demand coverage may reduce stockouts; check stockouts and paid sales after fresh supply checks.
Same-owner/category recovery probes for eligible failed contracts may improve outcomes without changing price caps; assess comparable closed and paid results.
The rating holdout surrogate reports lower MSE than baseline, but official stars mapping is unverified and the result is not causal; do not promote a rating policy.

market_research_published.summary: Keep the current research parameters and operating policy. Stockouts are elevated (44 in 60 minutes) against 51 units of stock, while shop sales and external trade activity remain substantial. However, defensive controls and unhealthy transport block restocking, so do not issue a stock-coverage operating intent until live guards permit it. Goods contracts convert poorly and are mostly above cap; retain the existing buyer settings and do not change the price cap. The challenger is not ready for promotion. Although the diversified plan has the strongest modeled supply-plan utility, execution remains guarded and its projection is not realized performance.
hypotheses: Low stock and repeated stockouts may support greater inventory coverage once live supply and cash guards clear; current controls are a counterexample to acting now.
Goods contract recovery routing may help, but weak goods conversion and mostly above-cap quotes do not justify changing price caps or settings without further comparable evidence.
The challenger’s observed reward exceeds the champion’s, but its 119 closed cases and 9 paid do not meet the mature-evaluation gate.

market_research_published.summary: Authorize bounded measurement-based stock coverage and buyer price-failure routing, but do not approve economic promotion or change trial parameters. Stock is low (51 units versus 237 median peer stock) with 41 stockouts in 60 minutes; the supply plan favors diversified stocking, though defensive/discoverability blocks remain. Buyer goods conversion is weak (4/36 closed orders paid in the recent 60 minutes), and 59/60 goods quotes were above cap. Keep the current operating policy and avoid treating routing as a price-cap exception. The challenger is not promotion-ready; the quality holdout is predictive, not causal, and official rank mapping remains unverified.
hypotheses: Bounded repeat-demand coverage may reduce stockouts and support shop outcomes; verify with subsequent stockouts and paid sales, accounting for supply blocks.

Routing repeated, comparable goods price failures to recovery probes may improve closed-order outcomes without changing price caps; current goods conversion and above-cap quotes are counterevidence to assuming broad improvement.
The quality surrogate has lower holdout MSE than baseline, but unverified official rank mapping and non-causal evidence do not justify profile promotion.

market_research_published.summary: Approve bounded operating responses: stockouts are elevated despite near-flat-to-slightly-rising market activity, and buyer recovery routing is justified by repeated above-cap failures. Keep operating policy and buyer parameters at baseline; the diversified supply plan has the highest supplied utility, but discovery and defensive/stale-control blocks require live checks. Do not promote the challenger: evaluation is not ready, and its apparent uplift lacks sufficient mature evidence.
hypotheses: A bounded repeat-demand coverage response may reduce stockouts; assess subsequent stockouts, paid sales, and capital exposure.
Routing qualifying failed contracts to recovery probes may help Buyer outcomes, but goods conversion remains low and most quotes exceed cap; do not relax price caps.
The challenger’s higher observed reward may not persist with mature evidence; hold promotion pending evaluator readiness.

market_research_published.summary: Approve bounded stock-coverage and buyer price-gap routing responses, while retaining the current operating policy and profile parameters. Stockouts (49 in 60 minutes) and 48 units of stock versus 198 median peer stock support a coverage response, though external trade rate is essentially flat and a discoverability block is recorded. Goods conversion is weak (5/43 closed orders paid) and 61/62 goods quotes were above cap; route qualifying repeated failures to recovery probes without changing the cap. Do not promote a challenger: evaluation is not ready and has only 9 paid challenger outcomes. The quality holdout is predictive, not causal, and official stars-rank mapping is unverified.
hypotheses: A bounded repeat-demand coverage response may reduce stockouts, subject to live supply, cash, and refund guards; flat external trade rate and the discoverability block are counterevidence to expanding inventory broadly.

Routing repeated, term-comparable goods price failures to recovery probes may improve learning without changing the price cap; above-cap quotes alone do not establish that any revised offer will convert.
The holdout predictive improvement does not establish causal star gains or verify the official stars-rank mapping.
